columns.headline: Chad vs Brad: 20 Meetings, Dead Even, Somebody Finally Blinks
columns.dek: The all-time series is tied 10-10, Chad has the league's biggest points total, and Brad is riding a three-game heater. ESPN likes Chad. Brad likes Brad.
body: The game of the week is Chad against Brad, and it isn't close as a choice. The all-time series is tied 10-10, which means twenty meetings have settled exactly nothing. Chad sits second at 8-4 with 744.8 points for, the biggest pile in the league, and a playoff chance of 87.65%. Brad is 6-6, seventh, on a W3 streak, and sitting at 43.48%, which is fantasy for "we'll see."

ESPN projects Chad at 118.01 to Brad's 98.4 and gives Chad a 60% win chance. That's the projection talking, not the verdict, and Brad will tell you the number undersells him the same way he insists his head isn't that big. Win this and the series finally has a leader. Lose it and Brad's heater goes back in the drawer with the rest of his 6-6 season.

The closest projection on the board is Jon against Ben, a gap of 0.99 with ESPN calling it 51% to 49%. Jon is first at 9-3 and projected for 102.86; Ben is tenth at 5-7 and projected for 101.87. So the league leader, the man with the most expensive weekly video budget in fantasy history, is projected to beat a 5-7 team by less than a point. Great production values, coin-flip product. Jon leads the series 3-2.

The biggest mismatch is Jared against Joe K, a projected gap of 22.65. Joe K is projected for 105.13 and a 64% win chance, which is ESPN trusting Joe K with something, a bold choice. Jared is 3-9, on an L2 skid, projected for 82.48, and staring at a 15.13% playoff chance. Joe K leads that series 13-7, so if Jared loses this one too, it's tradition, not news. If Joe K blows it, that's a whole different column.

Kris and Jeff are both 7-5 and both live in the playoff bubble, Kris fourth and Jeff sixth. ESPN has Jeff at 91.4 to Kris's 88.39, a 52% to 48% lean, and Jeff brings a W2 streak against Kris's L1. Kris leads the series 9-5 and has the points edge, 613.76 to 567.94, but neither of them is projected to clear the projected median of 100.01. Somebody wins ugly.

Joe G gets TJ, who is 8-4 and third. Joe G is projected for 101.98 and a 55% chance despite an L2 streak, and he leads the series 4-2. Down at the bottom, Collin is 2-10, alone in last, on an L3 run with a 4.35% playoff chance. ESPN still makes him a 51% favorite over Flanders, 100.66 to 99.35, which is either a sign of life or a projection system with a sense of humor. Flanders leads that series 9-5.

columns.headline: TJ Benches His Way Out of a Win as Chad Takes First Alone
columns.dek: TJ's best lineup beat Joe G and he didn't play it. Chad hung 49.38 on Brad and owns first place by himself. Jon fell off the top.
body: The week's closest game was also its dumbest. Joe G beat TJ 108.62 to 105.64, a 2.98-point margin, and TJ was the only loser in the league whose best lineup would have won. That lineup was 108.84. He left Tyrone Tracy Jr. on the bench with 8.20 and started Derrick Henry at running back, who returned 5.40 on a 17.37 projection. That is 3.20 points left on the pine in a game decided by less, which is dumb, plain and simple, and the league has signed off on the word.

The insult is that TJ still climbed. Drake Maye's 27.44 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 26.80 cleared the 101.55 median by 4.09, so he banked the side win and moved from third to second at 9-5, ahead of a three-way pile at the same record on points. Joe G leads that series 5-2 and gets no credit here either: Brock Purdy scored 12.02 on a 20.43 projection and Aaron Jones Sr. gave him 3.10 in the flex. Zay Flowers and his 23.70 did the rest, and Joe G sits fifth at 9-5.

The biggest beating belonged to Chad, who took Brad apart 107.20 to 57.82, a 49.38-point margin. Brad's 57.82 was the low score of the week by a mile, Bryce Young delivered 5.42 on a 17.66 projection, and Roschon Johnson added 1.30. His best lineup was 68.12, so there was no bench move hiding in there, just a bad roster having a bad day. Brad drops from seventh to ninth at 6-8, and Chad now leads the series 11-10. Chad, meanwhile, got 23.50 from Bucky Irving and 21.70 from Luther Burden III, survived Nico Collins scoring 1.60 on a 14.01 projection, and is alone in first at 10-4 with 852.00 points.

That top spot came at Jon's expense. Jon lost to Ben 96.08 to 85.28, finished 11th of 12 to miss the median too, and went 0-2 on the week, sliding from first to third. Kenneth Walker III scored 7.70 on a 17.74 projection in the flex and Juwan Johnson added 1.20 at tight end; even Jon's best lineup of 89.18 would have lost. Ben will take the win and the 3-3 series tie, but his 96.08 was still under the median, so he went 1-1 and stays tenth. Joe Burrow's 28.88 did the lifting while Jalen Coker gave him 1.40 on a 12.57 projection.

Flanders put up the high score of the week, 115.82, beat Collin, and jumped from eighth to sixth. He also had the best possible lineup of anyone at 137.82, because Omar Cooper Jr. scored 20.00 on his bench while Germie Bernard started at receiver for 4.20. He left 22.00 on the bench and won anyway, which is the most expensive way to win a fantasy game. Cam Skattebo's 18.60 on a 7.32 projection helped cover it. Collin got 23.80 from Tee Higgins and a donut at receiver from Garrett Wilson, started the best lineup he had, and still sits alone in last at 2-12. Flanders leads that series 10-5.

Joe K beat Jared 114.20 to 86.40, the second-best score of the week, and climbed from ninth to seventh. He did it while being dumb: Keon Coleman, projected for nothing, started in the flex and laid exactly the donut he was projected for, while Devaughn Vele scored 13.90 on the bench. Jameson Williams bailed him out with 23.60 on an 8.95 projection, which made Patrick Mahomes and his 6.00 survivable. Jared got a donut from Rashid Shaheed at receiver, but his entire bench scored nothing, so nothing on the bench would have saved him. He stays 11th at 3-11, and Joe K leads that series 14-7.

The best start of the week against projection went to Kris: Tony Pollard scored 35.00 on a 12.92 projection, beating it by 22.08, and Kris beat Jeff 110.62 to 92.72 to hold fourth at 9-5. He left Emanuel Wilson's 18.00 on the bench and won by 17.90, so nobody will ask. Jeff started George Kittle in the flex for a donut on a 13.95 projection and Terry McLaurin at receiver, projected for nothing, for another donut. Trey McBride's 22.10 could only do so much, his best lineup of 95.92 still lost, and Jeff falls from sixth to eighth. Kris leads that series 10-5.

columns.headline: Jon Loses His Way Into First as Brad Hangs 147.14 on Jared
columns.dek: Brad had the high score and the biggest beating, Kris lost by a hair with the winning lineup on his own bench, and Jon took first place with a loss.
body: Brad dropped 147.14 on Jared, the high score of the week and the biggest beating, a 69.76-point margin that stretches his series lead to 15-4. Bhayshul Tuten scored 22.70 on an 11.69 projection, and Brad's best possible lineup was 150.04, and he left only 2.90 on the bench. It moved him up exactly one spot, to seventh at 6-6, which tells you everything about the five weeks before it. Brad has always insisted his head isn't that big and his dick isn't that small, and a score like this does more for the second claim than the first. Jared took the other end of it: Bijan Robinson scored 6.30 on a 21.34 projection, Tyjae Spears added 1.30, and Kyle Pitts Sr.'s 20.50 was a lifeboat on a sunk ship. He falls two spots to 11th at 3-9.

Jon lost to TJ 101.60 to 95.42 and still took sole possession of first place at 9-3, because 95.42 cleared the 83.65 median and banked a win on the side. Kenneth Walker III scored 26.90 and DeVonta Smith 17.00, while Juwan Johnson at tight end and Antonio Williams at receiver each put up a donut. A big production budget, two blank frames, and a premiere that somehow lands in first place: that is the Jon video model in one week. TJ's win ran on Tre Tucker's 24.20 against an 8.59 projection, the best start of the week against projection, which covered for Derrick Henry's 4.50 on a 17.60 projection. TJ climbs to third at 8-4, and Jon still leads the series 5-2.

The closest game was Ben 83.72, Kris 82.10, a 1.62-point margin, and Kris has nobody to blame but Kris. His best lineup was 88.30, enough to win, and it left Woody Marks and his 9.10 on the bench while Rhamondre Stevenson took the flex for 3.60. Falling short of the median meant he lost twice in one afternoon. He slides from third to fourth and Ben takes the series lead, 9-7. Ben cleared the median by 0.07, which is not a victory so much as an administrative error in his favor.

Joe K missed that same median by 0.07, then lost to Jeff 100.30 to 83.58 and fell from seventh to ninth at 5-7. He did start the best lineup he had, so the blame goes to Patrick Mahomes, who scored 10.48 against an 18.77 projection, and to a roster where only Matthew Golden's 19.40 showed up for work. Jeff won while doing his best to give it away: C.J. Stroud scored 22.98 on his bench, Terry McLaurin started at receiver for 3.20 while Jakobi Meyers sat with 10.80, and Jeff left 15.48 behind and still won by 16.72. He leads that series 12-8.

Chad started the week in first place and finished it in second, losing to Flanders 104.50 to 83.24 despite 27.34 from Trevor Lawrence. Kyren Williams scored 8.20 on a 19.17 projection, Wan'Dale Robinson added 3.70 in the flex, and even Chad's best lineup of 92.94 would have lost, so there is no bench to blame. His 744.80 points lead the league, which makes him the highest-scoring team in the league and somehow not first in it. Flanders posted the second-best score of the week, jumped three spots to eighth, and got 20.20 from Germie Bernard against a 7.79 projection, despite Will Shipley laying a donut in the flex. Chad still leads that series 12-10.

Joe G beat Collin 78.66 to 69.14 with the tenth-best score of the week, below the median, with Mark Andrews adding 0.90 in the flex and Harold Fannin Jr. 1.40 at tight end. It is a win, it is 7-5, and it is fifth place, and it looks like a clerical error. Collin took the low score of the week and sits last at 2-10. He started Jordan Love for 20.24 while Tyler Shough scored 26.96 on the bench, but his best lineup of 77.16 would have lost anyway, so that is a footnote to a bad roster, not the story. Joe G leads that series 9-6.

columns.headline: Chad Flattens Joe G and Takes Over First Place
columns.dek: Chad posted the week's best score by a mile, Jon won with the tenth-best score and still slid out of first, and Collin left a winning quarterback on the bench.
body: Chad did not so much beat Joe G as file a noise complaint against him. The final was 155.24 to 68.26, a margin of 86.98, the highest and lowest scores of the week in the same box. Jahmyr Gibbs put up 35.20 and Christian Watson beat his projection by 17.78. The series now sits tied 11-11, and Chad leads the standings at 8-2, ahead of Jon on points. Even his worst lineup call was a rounding error: 1.40 points left on the bench.

Joe G, meanwhile, got 1.90 from CeeDee Lamb on a 15.46 projection, and RJ Harvey chipped in 0.70. His best possible lineup was 81.36, so no bench move was saving this one. He drops from third to fifth at 6-4, which is still a winning record, which is the nicest thing anyone can say about his Sunday.

Now the one that hurts. Collin lost the week's closest game to Jon, 81.54 to 74.42, by 7.12. He started Tyler Shough at quarterback, who finished at -0.16 on a 16.51 projection, while Jordan Love sat on his bench with 25.28. Collin's best lineup was 107.46, enough to win, which makes him the only loser this week who chose his loss. He left 33.04 on the pine and slides to last at 2-8.

Jon will take the win, and he should, because it was a heist. His 81.54 was tenth of 12, well under the 100.25 median, and his bench produced exactly 0.00. Parker Washington's 27.40 carried the lineup. Jon went 1-1 on the week, and he slid from first to second at 8-2, behind Chad on points. Jon leads that series 4-3.

Jeff beat Brad 108.36 to 100.70 despite starting a quarterback who scored 0.00 on an 18.17 projection, with C.J. Stroud and his 20.94 sitting on the bench. Jayden Daniels and his 32.26 covered for it. Jeff jumps from ninth to sixth. Brad got 26.90 from Isaiah Likely and 1.10 from Carnell Tate, beat the 100.25 median by 0.45, and still lost. He stays eighth and still leads Jeff 10-7 in the series, for what that is worth this week.

TJ owns the start of the week: Drake Maye put up 39.46 on an 18.47 projection, beating it by 20.99, and TJ beat Ben 123.56 to 99.80. Ben missed the median by 0.45, got 1.10 from David Montgomery, and fell from seventh to tenth. Joe K handled Kris 124.88 to 105.50 and climbed from tenth to seventh. Kris left MarShawn Lloyd's 16.20 on the bench, but his best lineup was 124.00, still short, so blame the opponent and not the clipboard.

Down in the cellar, Flanders beat Jared 96.34 to 85.92 while getting 0.00 from tight end Kenyon Sadiq, and that was enough to climb out of last to eleventh. Jared got 1.50 from Deebo Samuel Sr. and fell from sixth to ninth. Jared still leads that series 9-8.
